html:
The Mueda massacre took place on 16 June 1960 at Mueda in northern Mozambique, when Portuguese troops fired on a crowd of Makonde villagers who had gathered to press the authorities over pay and independence.

The crowd had come to hear the response to requests by local leaders. When the governor had the leaders arrested, the crowd protested, and the soldiers opened fire. The number of dead is disputed, from a few dozen by some accounts to hundreds by others.

The massacre convinced many that peaceful protest was useless. The Makonde plateau became the first base of FRELIMO's guerrillas in the war of independence, which began in the same region in 1964. It is remembered in Mozambique each June.
sum: The Mueda massacre took place on 16 June 1960 at Mueda in northern Mozambique, when Portuguese troops fired on a crowd of Makonde villagers who had gathered to press the authorities over pay and independence.
